question: In the EU, a number of occupational groups carry out activities classified as toxic, arduous and hazardous, especially in sectors such as the chemical and refining industries. Given the obvious physical and mental burden of those jobs, workers in those areas need to be able to take early retirement.

That requirement is backed up by studies such as the scientific survey carried out in 2023 by the University of Zaragoza (Spain) and the Sindicato de Trabajadores (Workers’ Union), which demonstrate the debilitating nature of those jobs. Against that backdrop: 1.
What specific plan does the Commission have to address employment circumstances for workers in the chemical and refining industries, whose tasks are considered toxic, arduous and hazardous?
Is the Commission working to establish EU legislation to give that group access to early retirement, in line with individual Member States’ laws?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.4.2024) 1. The health and safety of workers in the chemical and refining industries is governed by several EU occupational safety and health directives, such as the Framework Directive1, the Carcinogens, Mutagens and Reprotoxic Substances Directive (CMRD)2 and the Chemical Agents Directive (CAD)3.

They place specific obligations on the employers to ensure workers’ safety and health in every aspect related to work and set minimum requirements that relate to the assessment of risks to which workers are or might be exposed, training, information of workers, preventive and protective measures.
As regards the CMRD and CAD specifically, occupational limit values for workers’ exposure are set to protect workers from the adverse and toxic effect of chemicals.

One of the three crosscutting strategic objectives of the EU Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Strategic Framework4 is the improvement of the prevention of work-related diseases with the continuous update of the EU OSH directives dealing with hazardous substances. 2.

The EU supports and complements the activities of Member States in social protection, primarily through facilitating mutual learning, analysis and policy guidance. However, the provisions adopted at EU level shall not affect the right of Member States to define fundamental principles of their social security systems and must not significantly affect their financial equilibrium.
5 The Commission therefore does not plan to propose EU legislation providing and determining early retirement for specific workers in the chemical and refining industries sectors.
1 Directive 89/391/EEC on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health of

workers at work, OJ L 183, 29.6.1989, p. 1. 2 Directive 2009/148/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 November 2009 on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work, OJ L 330, 16.12.2009, p. 28.

3 Council Directive 98/24/EC of 7 April 1998 on the protection of the health and safety of workers from the risks related to chemical agents at work (fourteenth individual Directive within the meaning of Article 16(1) of Directive 89/391/EEC), OJ L 131, 5.5.1998, p. 11. 4 EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at Work 2021-2027, COM/2021/323 final, available at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?
uri=CELEX%3A52021DC0323&qid=1626089672913#PP1Contents . 5 Article 153 (4) of the Treaty of Functioning of the European Union.
